key_insight: CalTennis is a major new benchmark for monocular-to-3D human pose estimation in real-world sports, providing synchronized multi-view tennis video at a scale far beyond prior datasets. It enables more reliable evaluation of 3D pose methods under challenging in-the-wild conditions.
problem_solved: Existing datasets for 3D human pose estimation are either too small, too controlled, or lack synchronized multi-view coverage in realistic settings. This paper addresses the need for a large-scale, in-the-wild benchmark to evaluate monocular-to-3D pose methods on complex tennis motion.
method: Collected 11M+ frames (51 hours) of tennis practice and match play from 40 players.
Captured footage using 2-6 synchronized cameras at 60 Hz to provide multi-view video for pose benchmarking.
Built a benchmark designed specifically for evaluating monocular-to-3D pose estimation in realistic, dynamic sports scenes.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CalTennis offers a much tougher and more realistic testbed for 3D pose estimation methods. It can help reveal failure cases, improve generalization, and drive progress toward robust pose estimation in unconstrained environments.
